title: Alternating Groups III
statement:
Tiles stand in a circle. `colors[i]` is the colour of tile `i`: `0` for red, `1` for blue. With `n = colors.length`, tile `n - 1` and tile `0` are neighbours.

An **alternating group** of size `k` is a stretch of `k` consecutive tiles around the circle in which every two tiles that are next to each other within the stretch have different colours. Groups are told apart by their first tile, so for a given `k` at most one group starts at each tile (`k` is always below `n`, so a group never laps the circle).

Process `queries` in order:

- `[1, size]`: report how many alternating groups have exactly `size` tiles.
- `[2, index, color]`: set `colors[index]` to `color` (the tile may already have that colour).

Return the reports of the type-1 queries, in order.
constraints: A type-1 query is [1, size] with 3 <= size <= colors.length - 1
A type-2 query is [2, index, color] with 0 <= index <= colors.length - 1 and color 0 or 1
notes:
## Intuition

Edge `e` joins tile `e` to tile `(e + 1) % n`; it is a **break** when both tiles share a colour. A group alternates exactly when none of its `size - 1` inner edges is a break. Cutting the circle at every break leaves maximal alternating **runs**, and a run of `L >= size` tiles holds `L - size + 1` groups. So a query needs (tiles in runs with `L >= size`) minus `size - 1` times (number of such runs): two Fenwick trees indexed by run length give both in O(log n), where the brute force re-checks every start in O(n · size).

Recolouring a tile flips the two edges beside it: a new break splits a run, a vanished one merges two. Locating them needs the nearest breaks on each side, an ordered-set lookup that a third Fenwick tree, over edges, answers by descending to the k-th break.

## Approach

1. `marks` holds 1 at every break; `runCount` and `runTiles` count runs and their tiles by length.
2. `gap(from, to)` is the length of the run between consecutive breaks `from` and `to`, or `n` when they are the same break.
3. `flipEdge(edge)` sets `sign` to +1 (new break) or -1 (vanished), finds `prev` and `next`, the nearest other breaks, and swaps run `prev → next` for runs `prev → edge` and `edge → next`, or back. With no other break, the circle is one run of `n` tiles.
4. Build by flipping every edge that starts as a break.
5. `[1, size]`: answer `tiles - (size - 1) * runs`, or `n` when there is no break.
6. `[2, index, color]`: if the colour changes, recolour and flip the edges on both sides of `index`.

## Example 1, step by step

`colors = [0,1,1,0,1]` has one break, edge 1, so one run of 5 tiles. `[2,1,0]` gives `[0,0,1,0,1]`: `flipEdge(0)` adds a break, splitting the run into 4 and 1 tiles; `flipEdge(1)` removes edge 1's break, merging them into one run of 5 after edge 0. `[1,4]`: `runs = 1`, `tiles = 5`, answer `5 - 3 * 1 = 2`.

## Complexity

- Time: O((n + q) log n): each edge flip and query does a fixed number of Fenwick operations.
- Space: O(n) for the three trees.

## Pitfalls

- The circle wraps: the nearest break may lie across index 0, and edge `n - 1` joins the last tile to the first.
- One break means one run of `n` tiles, not 0; no break means all `n` starts work.
- Skip recolours that keep the colour; flipping the edges anyway corrupts the trees.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `marks`, `breaks` | Fenwick tree over edges with 1 per break, and the number of breaks |
| `runCount`, `runTiles` | Fenwick trees over run lengths: runs and their tiles |
| `highBit` | largest power of two not above `n`, the first step of the k-th search |
| `sign` | +1 for a new break, -1 for a vanished one |
| `below`, `prev`, `next` | breaks before the edge, and the nearest breaks on each side |
| `runs`, `tiles` | runs with at least `size` tiles, and their total tiles |

narration.3: Fenwick tree over edges: index edge + 1 holds 1 when that edge is a break, meaning its two tiles share a colour.
narration.4: Fenwick tree over run lengths: how many alternating runs have each length.
narration.5: A second tree over run lengths: the total tiles of the runs of each length.
narration.6: breaks counts the break edges currently marked.
narration.8: highBit becomes the largest power of two not above n; the k-th search starts there.
narration.10: Fenwick update: add delta to every node whose range covers index.
narration.14: Fenwick prefix sum: add the nodes that together cover 1..index.
narration.17: findBreak(k) uses the tree as an ordered set and returns the edge of the k-th break from the left.
narration.20: Jump right while the breaks skipped so far are still fewer than k.
narration.22: Those breaks are passed, so fewer remain to find.
narration.25: The k-th break sits at 1-based index pos + 1, which is edge number pos.
narration.28: Mark or unmark the edge in the tree and keep the count in step.
narration.31: Tiles in the run after break from up to break to; the same break twice means the whole circle, n tiles.
narration.33: Add (sign +1) or remove (sign -1) one run of this length in both trees.
narration.37: The edge has just flipped: +1 if it is now a break, -1 if it no longer is.
narration.38: A vanishing break is unmarked first, so the searches below only see the other breaks.
narration.39: With no other break, this edge alone turns the whole circle into one run of n tiles, which appears or disappears with it.
narration.42: Count the other breaks that lie before this edge.
narration.43: The nearest break before it, wrapping round to the last break when none is before.
narration.44: The nearest break after it, wrapping round to the first break when none is after.
narration.45: A new break removes the run from prev to next (a vanishing one restores it)...
narration.46: ...and adds the two shorter runs on either side of the edge (or removes them).
narration.49: A new break is marked only after the searches.
narration.51: Build the trees by turning on every edge that starts as a break.
narration.58: Runs with at least size tiles: all runs minus those shorter than size.
narration.59: The total tiles in those runs.
narration.60: A run of L tiles holds L - size + 1 groups; with no break at all, every one of the n starts works.
narration.63: Recolouring a tile with its own colour changes nothing.
narration.65: A new colour flips the edge on the tile's left...
narration.69: The reports of the counting queries, in order.
